subject: Capacity buckets + seat trim proposal — HealthNova
messages:
From: Sonia Patel <sonia@healthnova.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@healthnova.com
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging options — we need a lower run-rate + flexibility

Karthik — thanks again for the demo last week. We like Redwood's performance, but our CFO pushed back on the current run-rate for the POC and asked whether theres a way to: 1) reduce the monthly committed spend (were OK trimming seats), 2) buy predictable inference capacity in smaller buckets rather than a single large reserve, and 3) optionally add higher-throughput lanes for spikes.

Can you sketch a configuration that gives us: a cheaper baseline, a clear upgrade path for end-of-quarter spikes, and one-line guidance on how model quantization or batching would change effective cost? Procurement will need a simple comparison table and a notional SOW.

— Sonia
VP Product, HealthNova

---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Sonia Patel <sonia@healthnova.com>
Cc: procure@healthnova.com, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options — we need a lower run-rate + flexibility

Sonia — really appreciate the clarity. High level proposal inline below; attaching a simple model (pricing_model_v2.xlsx) and a draft SOW.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Baseline: Trim seats from 30 -> 18 for the POC and convert the rest to a small dedicated capacity bucket (2 RU-equivalent GPUs) for predictable throughput. This reduces committed monthly by ~35%.
- Spike capacity: Offer 'burst lanes' purchased as hourly credits or a weekly short-term top-up at 2x baseline price (auto-billed, optional).
- Add-ons: Advanced KV caching + autoscaler preserves latency for bursts — priced as a small % premium.
- Quality tradeoffs: 8-bit quantization with batching reduces per-token cost by ~40% for LLM-2 style models, but may increase latency variance; we outline recommended prompts to mitigate hallucination risk.

Why this mix: seats map to steady-day-to-day concurrency (developer/admin seats + sandbox); capacity buckets map to steady inference pipelines (API backends). Separating them lets you keep a low committed baseline while still getting throughput predictability for non-interactive jobs.

Next steps I suggest:
1) We send a one-page comparison (baseline vs trimmed seats + small bucket vs full reserve) for your finance team — I can produce that by Monday.
2) If procurement is agreeable, we will embed a 3-month opt-in for burst lanes in the SOW, and include a brief SLA for availability of burst capacity.
3) Lauren will weigh in on discounting for committed dollars and provide a final numbers table.

Ive ccd Lauren — Lauren, can you confirm whether we can offer a 10% sticker discount on the trimmed-commit baseline and what additional uplift wed need to maintain margin if HealthNova wants a staffed onboarding window?

Thanks — Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: pricing_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
Attachment: SOW-draft-HealthNova.docx (doc stub)

---
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Sonia Patel <sonia@healthnova.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>, procure@healthnova.com
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options — we need a lower run-rate + flexibility

Sonia — quick note on discounts and bundling. We can do a structured discount ladder tied to committed dollars:
- Commit $40k/mo: 10% off list (this is the trimmed baseline Karthik suggests).
- Commit $80k/mo: 16% off list + 1 month onboarding credit.
- Multi-quarter commit (6 months+): +2% (cumulative) and reduced burst rate from 2x -> 1.6x.

To preserve gross margin wed need the following concessions: either a 12-month minimum term for the $40k baseline, or an increased per-token surcharge on burst lanes. If you want us to include managed onboarding, assume an additional one-time Professional Services fee (line-item in SOW).

Rachel — note procurement will ask for a short SOW and a single-sheet table comparing total cost for P50 and P95 throughput under the three configurations. Can you help populate the SOW with the service hours for onboarding and post-launch support?

— Lauren
Director, Commercial Operations

From: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
To: Sonia Patel <sonia@healthnova.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@healthnova.com
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options — we need a lower run-rate + flexibility

Hi Sonia — looping back with the SOW and a one-page comparison. Ive attached a draft SOW (SOW-draft-HealthNova.docx) and pasted a condensed table below so procurement can quickly see the delta.

Condensed comparison (monthly):
- Option A (Trimmed baseline): $38,500/mo commit — 18 seats + small 2-RU bucket. Estimated P95 cost with 8-bit quantization: $45k/mo. 10% discount applied.
- Option B (Mid reserve): $74,000/mo commit — 30 seats + 4-RU bucket. 16% discount + 1 onboarding credit. P95 estimate: $86k/mo.
- Option C (Full reserve): $140,000/mo commit — 50 seats + 12-RU bucket. 20% discount on list for 12-month term. P95 estimate: $155k/mo.

Burst lanes: priced at 2x baseline per-hour outside committed capacity. If you sign a 6-month commit we can reduce burst lane multiplier to 1.6x.

Attached SOW includes: scope, onboarding hours (40h dedicated), support SLAs, billing cadence, and an optional embedding-refresh run (one-time).

If procurement wants a redline I can accept a procurement-friendly payment clause (Net45) and a pilot clause limiting liability during the POC. Let me know preferred billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and I will send a cleaned proposal.

Best — Rachel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOW-draft-HealthNova.docx (doc stub)
